lines: Riley Chen
+1 (555) 010-7731 | riley.chen@example.com | example.com/in/riley-chen
Date of birth: 2 Nov 1996 | Nationality: American
EDUCATION
Northfield School of Management | MBA | Metro City, USA | Sep 2023 - Jun 2025
Lakeview University | B.A. in Economics | Lake City, USA | Sep 2014 - Jun 2018
EXPERIENCE
Harbor Payments | Associate Product Manager Intern | Metro City, USA | Jun 2024 - Aug 2024
- Improved checkout conversion by 35% after replacing the three-step flow with a one-page flow for all merchants.
- Wrote the requirements and success metrics for dispute self-service, aligning engineering, risk and support; the team shipped it two weeks ahead of plan.
- Interviewed 25 merchants and analysed six months of chargeback data to size annual chargeback losses at 1.1 million dollars, the business case that set the next quarter's roadmap priority.
- Ran weekly triage with engineering and support, closing 140 onboarding tickets over the summer and cutting the open-ticket queue by half.
- Measured the onboarding redesign by comparing merchants who opted into the new flow with those who stayed on the old one.
- Redesigned merchant onboarding around a single verification step, cutting median time to first payment from 9 days to 4 across 2,300 new merchants in the pilot region.
Crestline Logistics | Operations Analyst | Lake City, USA | Mar 2019 - Aug 2023
- Cut late deliveries from 11% to 7% by excluding weather-delayed shipments from the on-time calculation.
- Cut warehouse pick errors 30% at two sites by redesigning slotting rules with the floor supervisors and retraining 45 pickers on the new layout.
- Coordinated the quarterly S&OP review across sales, finance and operations and prepares the forecast pack for each meeting.
- Led the rollout of a route-planning tool to 3 depots, training 60 drivers and dispatchers and saving 1,800 driver hours a year.
PROJECTS
Campus Food Rescue App | Product Lead | Student Venture | Oct 2023 - Present
- Launched a surplus-food pickup app to 3,100 students with two dining halls, redistributing 9 tonnes of food that would have been thrown away in its first year.
- Launched pickup reminders after 60 user interviews showed students missed pickup windows; weekly active users grew from 400 to 1,150 over the following term.
- Set up a volunteer shift system with two dining halls, filling 95% of pickup slots each week and cutting staff cover shifts from 10 to 2 a week.
MBA Consulting Practicum | Team Lead | Regional Hospital Network | Jan 2024 - May 2024
- Held weekly working sessions with clinic managers on outpatient scheduling across the network.
- Patient intake at 4 clinics was mapped and the intake form was shortened, with the changes adopted by front-desk staff.
- Halved the time it takes a new merchant to receive a first payment, across 2,300 merchants, by redesigning onboarding.
SKILLS
Product: roadmapping, A/B testing, user interviews, requirements writing
Tools: Jira, Amplitude, Excel

items.says: The operations-to-product narrative is not explicitly framed.
items.because: Recruiters currently have to infer the transition into product management.

items.says: The relationship among the Harbor checkout and onboarding bullets is unclear.
items.because: Several bullets appear to describe overlapping initiatives without a clear problem, intervention, evaluation method and result sequence.

items.says: Both education entries may not need location details.
items.because: That space could be used for relevant accomplishments.

items.says: Meaningful academic distinctions are not included.
items.because: Honors, scholarships, class rank or particularly relevant coursework could add differentiation if available.

items.says: The header lacks a clear product-management title or positioning line.
items.because: The current header does not immediately establish the target role.

items.says: The portfolio or LinkedIn URL should be verified as valid and professionally complete.
items.because: Links should be included only when they are real and current.

items.says: The résumé includes date of birth and nationality.
items.because: They are irrelevant to product hiring and can create avoidable bias or compliance concerns.

items.says: The MBA entry lacks substantive product, technology, entrepreneurship, analytics or leadership involvement.
items.because: The MBA should help explain the product transition and differentiate the candidate.

items.says: The 35% checkout-conversion result has no measurement period.
items.because: The current wording does not provide enough measurement context.

items.says: The 35% checkout-conversion result has no sample size.
items.because: The current wording invites skepticism about the scope of the result.

items.says: The checkout bullet does not identify whether the result came from an A/B test, controlled rollout or before-and-after comparison.
items.because: Product hiring managers will want to understand experimentation and attribution.

items.says: The bullet does not say whether 35% is a relative or percentage-point improvement.
items.because: The meaning of the reported conversion increase is ambiguous.

items.says: The phrase “for all merchants” sounds unusually broad and is not substantiated.
items.because: That scope is difficult to credit for a summer intern project without more detail.

items.says: The bullet may overstate that the redesign caused the entire conversion improvement.
items.because: A simple before-and-after comparison would not establish definitive causality.

items.says: The ownership boundary for the requirements is unclear.
items.because: The bullet does not distinguish personally owning the requirements from supporting their development.

items.says: The meaning of “shipped two weeks ahead of plan” is unclear.
items.because: It could refer to engineering completion, release date or the broader launch.

items.says: The bullet lacks a measurable customer or operational outcome after launch.
items.because: Customer impact and product judgment are stronger evidence than delivery speed alone.

items.says: “Analysed” uses British spelling while the résumé otherwise uses American context and terminology.
items.because: The résumé should use one spelling convention consistently.

items.says: The currency of the 1.1 million-dollar estimate is unclear.
items.because: The financial estimate needs a defined currency.

items.says: The loss estimate is not identified as annualized exposure, actual historical losses or projected savings opportunity.
items.because: Product managers need to distinguish observed losses from projected opportunity.

items.says: The connection among the research, business case and roadmap decision is imprecise.
items.because: The bullet should show more clearly how the analysis changed prioritization.

items.says: It is unclear whether Riley personally resolved 140 tickets or coordinated their resolution.
items.because: The current wording does not establish the ownership boundary.

items.says: The kinds of onboarding problems represented by the tickets are not stated.
items.because: Connecting them to recurring product problems would strengthen the product relevance.

items.says: The ticket volume is too central to the achievement.
items.because: The bullet currently reads more like support operations than product management.

items.says: The bullet does not explain why an opt-in comparison was appropriate or acknowledge its limitations.
items.because: Self-selection can weaken the validity of the comparison.

items.says: The comparison is not clearly identified as observational rather than randomized.
items.because: An opt-in comparison is not necessarily an A/B test or definitive causal evidence.

items.says: The bullet describes a method without stating an outcome.
items.because: It should support the onboarding achievement rather than appear as an unrelated project.

items.says: The measurement bullet is separated from the onboarding result it evaluates.
items.because: Placing the bullets together would make their relationship clearer.

items.says: The strongest onboarding result is buried late in the Harbor role.
items.because: The compelling 9-to-4-day result should be one of the first bullets.

items.says: The bullet does not clarify what Riley personally changed in the onboarding redesign.
items.because: The work could have involved workflow, verification, requirements, rollout or coordination.

items.says: The pilot scope and comparison basis are unclear.
items.because: The bullet does not say whether the result was measured against a baseline or control group.

items.says: The causal wording may be too definitive if the result came from a nonrandomized opt-in comparison.
items.because: Observational comparisons do not establish definitive causal evidence.

items.says: The bullet presents a changed calculation as a reduction in late deliveries.
items.because: Excluding weather-delayed shipments changes the measurement method rather than clearly improving operational performance.

items.says: Riley's analytical contribution to the slotting redesign is unclear.
items.because: The bullet does not distinguish Riley's work from the supervisors' and pickers' implementation work.

items.says: The bullet does not state whether the 30% error reduction was sustained over a defined period.
items.because: A measurement period would provide context for the result.

items.says: The warehouse-error achievement should appear earlier in the role.
items.because: It has a clear intervention and measurable result.

items.says: “Prepares” is in present tense even though the role is in the past.
items.because: The bullet tense is inconsistent with the employment dates.

items.says: Riley's role in the S&OP process is unclear.
items.because: The bullet does not distinguish coordination, analysis, forecasting, presentation or decision support.

items.says: The S&OP bullet states responsibilities without a business consequence.
items.because: It does not show what changed because of Riley's work.

items.says: The nature of Riley's leadership on the route-planning tool is unclear.
items.because: The bullet does not distinguish implementation, requirements gathering, rollout, training or adoption work.

items.says: The 1,800 annual hours are not identified as measured, estimated or projected savings.
items.because: The basis of the savings claim needs clarification.

items.says: The bullet gives training volume but no adoption or utilization rate.
items.because: Actual adoption could be more persuasive than training volume alone.

items.says: The route-planning achievement should be placed nearer the top of the role.
items.because: It is strong evidence of implementation, change management and technology adoption.

items.says: The Campus Food Rescue role is presented too much like a student project.
items.because: It needs to establish substantial product ownership.

items.says: Riley's role in the app launch is unclear.
items.because: The bullet does not identify ownership of product definition, research, design, partnerships or operations.

items.says: “To 3,100 students” does not distinguish availability, registered users or marketing reach.
items.because: App users need to be separated from total student reach.

items.says: The 9-tonne figure is not identified as measured or estimated.
items.because: The basis of the impact figure is unclear.

items.says: The weekly-active-user increase is not clearly distinguished as direct feature impact or growth merely observed after launch.
items.because: The bullet has causal ambiguity.

items.says: “Following term” is an imprecise measurement window.
items.because: A defined time period would make the result clearer.

items.says: The feature discovery and iteration process is not fully described.
items.because: This is the clearest discovery-to-feature-to-outcome example and could show more of the product process.

items.says: Riley's ownership of the volunteer shift system is unclear.
items.because: The bullet does not distinguish designing the system, implementing it or manually coordinating volunteers.

items.says: The reduction from 10 to 2 staff cover shifts is not clearly shown as a direct result of the system.
items.because: The bullet has causal ambiguity.

items.says: The bullet is overly operations-focused.
items.because: Its product value should be framed through workflow design, user needs and adoption.

items.says: The working sessions do not identify the product or operational problem being addressed.
items.because: The bullet describes activity without establishing its purpose.

items.says: The working sessions have no stated output or impact.
items.because: A product résumé should show the requirements, redesign, prioritization, implementation plan or decision that resulted.

items.says: The patient-intake work has no quantified improvement.
items.because: Time saved, fields removed, completion rate, staff adoption or error reduction would strengthen the result.

items.says: Riley's contribution to mapping and redesigning intake is unclear.
items.because: The bullet does not establish what Riley personally owned.

items.says: The bullet does not explain how staff adoption was verified.
items.because: It simply states that the changes were adopted.

items.says: The merchant-onboarding result duplicates the Harbor Payments onboarding bullet.
items.because: It can look like copied content, fabrication or careless editing.

items.says: The bullet refers to merchants under a regional hospital project.
items.because: The content is misplaced and makes the practicum appear unreliable.

items.says: The skills categories do not distinguish product methods and technical or analytical tools clearly enough.
items.because: The categories should communicate both product methods and tools more clearly.

items.says: The A/B testing skill is not fully supported by the experience bullets.
items.because: The résumé shows an opt-in comparison that was not necessarily an A/B test.

items.says: Several common APM terms are missing or underrepresented.
items.because: Product discovery, prioritization, product analytics, experiment design, launch management, stakeholder management, feature adoption and product strategy could improve searchability when truthful.

items.says: The tools list is limited and may omit relevant tools used in the projects or internships.
items.because: Additional tools could support the target role when they reflect genuine experience.
